Early second-look tympanoplasty can help reduce the conversion rate from open mastoid surgery (modified radical mastoidectomy) by allowing for easier removal of any recurrent or residual disease that may have been missed during the initial procedure. This approach enables surgeons to take a more targeted and less invasive approach, reducing the need for a major surgical intervention.

While early second-look tympanoplasty is generally safe and effective in treating cholesteatoma, its benefits are most significant when combined with other factors such as proper patient selection, careful preoperative planning, and adequate postoperative care.
